newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria holding to buy ailing state Yambol bank.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria holding to buy ailing state Yambol bank.

text.p: The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) said on Tuesday it has allowed a local insurance holding structure to buy the ailing state-owned Yambol bank, in receivership since September, for 3.8 billion levs.

"The BNB board decided to allow joint stock companies Bulgaria Holding, Energia Insurance and Bulgaria Insurance and Reinsurance to acquire 80, 10 and 10 percent of the voting shares of the Yambol bank, respectively," a BNB statement said.
The holding would invest 3.8 billion levs to raise the bank's capital to 3.813 billion levs, buying out a new issue of voting shares.
The Yambol bank would be renamed to Bulgaria Invest commercial bank and the BNB would lift its receivership restrictions from it following the acquisition, the BNB said.
The current 13 million lev capital of the Yambol bank is almost fully owned by Bulgaria's Bank Consolidation Company (BCC), which manages state equity in local commercial banks.
The 3.8 billion lev investment was large enough to cover the Yambol bank's debts and to allow it to resume operations, a BNB official told Reuters.
The Yambol bank has been the second local bank after the Bobovdol bank which the BNB has sought to close down three years ago and its operations have been effectively curbed by the BNB since then.

The BNB put the Yambol bank in receivership on September 23, 1996 due to a danger of insolvency, citing a capital to risk assets ratio of minus 15 percent. An insolvency suit was filed a month later. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 911 88
